title: 11 Upper-Back Exercises, Ranked
caption: Which upper-back exercise would you put at #1? This ranking favors stable setups, consistent reps, and straightforward weight increases. Your equipment and comfort matter, too. Save it for your next pull day.
reference: 13 screenshots supplied by the user, Blue Bro upper-back exercise ranking. Cover followed by #11 through #1. Original exercise order preserved; wording rewritten. Ranking is the reference creator's practical assessment, not a proven hierarchy of muscle growth.

items.name: Face Pulls
items.body:
Useful as an accessory, but not our first pick
for heavy upper-back work. Loading can get awkward.

items.name: Suspension Row
items.body:
A simple place to start with bodyweight rows.
Progression takes more setup as you get stronger.

items.name: DB Bent-Over Row
items.body:
Two free weights, no chest support.
It's easy to let body movement take over the rep.

items.name: Seal Row
items.body:
Chest support is a plus. The trade-off?
Bench height and clearance can make setup awkward.

items.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
items.body:
A classic row with more demand on your torso.
As the weight climbs, keep momentum in check.

items.name: Wide-Grip Cable Row
items.body:
A solid option, but your torso still needs to brace.
Heavier reps can turn into rocking without control.

items.name: Dumbbell Upper Row
items.body:
Chest support helps keep the reps steady.
Setup can be fiddly, but a bench and dumbbells work.

items.name: Smith Machine Rows
items.body:
The guided bar takes balance out of the equation.
You still need to hold your torso in position.

items.name:
Chest-Supported
Machine Row
items.body:
Chest support and a guided path keep things simple.
Easy weight changes help you track your progress.

items.name:
Chest-Supported
T-Bar Row
items.body:
A strong pick for a stable, heavy row.
Keep your chest on the pad and build the load steadily.

items.name: Kelso Shrugs
items.body:
Our top pick for focused shoulder-blade movement.
Keep your arms straight and squeeze your blades together.

sources.supports: Chest pad contact, torso stabilization demand without pad, controlled return. Mechanical support claims only; does not validate ranking.
Different back exercises activate different muscles; acute EMG cannot establish this 11-exercise hypertrophy ranking. Avoid calling lower ranks ineffective or number one universally best.
